name: Ruy Lopez
white: Use c3 and d4 to build a broad center while the bishop keeps pressure along the queenside diagonal.
black: Use …b5 for space and time …d5 or …c5 to challenge the center.
mistake: Avoid assuming the bishop on b5 already wins the e5-pawn.

variations.name: Marshall Attack
variations.source: Ruy Lopez: Marshall Attack, Main Line, Spassky Variation

name: Italian Game
white: Develop Bc4 toward f7. Decide between quiet d3 and preparing the central break d4.
black: Develop quickly and contest d4. In the Two Knights, meet Ng5 by opening the center with …d5.
mistake: Before attacking f7, check whether the king is safe and the center can open.

variations.name: Two Knights Defense
variations.source: Italian Game: Two Knights Defense, Knorre Variation

name: Giuoco Piano
white: Play c3 when it supports d4, then recapture in a way that keeps development moving.
black: Use …Nf6 and central counterplay to prevent White from keeping both central pawns unchallenged.
mistake: Check the forcing …Bb4+ after an early central exchange.

name: Giuoco Pianissimo
white: Use d3, c3, and Nbd2 to support the center before choosing when to play d4.
black: Preserve the bishop with …a6 if needed and compare …d5 with slower piece maneuvers.
mistake: An early wing pawn advance can leave your king exposed before you have built pressure.

name: Two Knights Defense
white: Compare the forcing Ng5 with quiet development after d3. Calculate Black's counterplay before taking on f7.
black: Use …d5 against Ng5. In the main line, …Na5 gains time against the bishop and leads to active development.
mistake: The natural …Nxd5 can allow Nxf7 and a sustained attack.

variations.name: Polerio Defense
variations.source: Italian Game: Two Knights Defense, Knorre Variation

name: Scotch Game
white: Open the center with d4 and use rapid development to exploit the resulting space.
black: Attack the centralized knight and play actively before White can consolidate.
mistake: Exchanging on c6 can give Black the bishop pair and a useful center.

name: Four Knights Game
white: Use the bishops to set the character of the game after developing both knights.
black: Maintain central balance, then look for a central break or an active bishop move.
mistake: Symmetric development can hide tactics once the center opens.

variations.name: Spanish Variation
variations.source: Four Knights Game: Spanish Variation, Symmetrical Variation

name: Vienna Game
white: Develop Nc3 to support e4 and keep the f-pawn available for a kingside initiative.
black: Develop with …Nf6 or …Nc6 and hit the center before a kingside attack gathers momentum.
mistake: After an early f4, calculate …d5 before assuming a pawn can be kept.

name: King's Gambit
white: Offer the f-pawn for central influence and an open f-file. Develop before trying to recover it.
black: Decide whether to accept, decline with a developing move, or challenge immediately with …d5.
mistake: Moving the f-pawn weakens the diagonal to your king. Calculate checks before opening it.

name: Danish Gambit
white: Trade queenside pawns for two active bishops and fast access to f7.
black: Return material when it allows central development or an exchange of queens.
mistake: A pawn lead has little value if your king remains in an open center.

name: Evans Gambit
white: Offer b4 to move the bishop away, gain time with c3, and expand with d4.
black: Choose whether to accept and where to retreat, then contest d4 before White's attack is established.
mistake: When you accept, returning a pawn can be the fastest route to safe development.

name: Bishop's Opening
white: Develop Bc4 before committing the g1-knight; choose between a quiet center and f4.
black: Pressure e4 with …Nf6 and use …c6 or …d5 when the timing works.
mistake: An early queen attack can lose time if Black develops with a threat.

name: Sicilian Defense
white: Use d4 to open the center or choose a quieter structure with Nc3 or c3. Plan around Black's central breaks.
black: Trade the c-pawn for White's d-pawn and use the half-open c-file and central majority for counterplay.
mistake: Attack on the wing only after accounting for …d5 and the open c-file.

variations.name: Dragon Variation
variations.source: Sicilian Defense: Dragon Variation, Yugoslav Attack, Topalov Variation

variations.name: Sveshnikov Variation
variations.source: Sicilian Defense: Lasker-Pelikan Variation, Sveshnikov Variation, Peresypkin's Sacrifice

name: French Defense
white: Use space from e5 or seek piece activity in the Exchange. Protect d4 when it is the base of your chain.
black: Challenge d4 with …c5 and find a role for the light-squared bishop. Time …f6 against e5.
mistake: An attack without support for d4 can allow the entire center to collapse.

variations.name: Classical Variation
variations.source: French Defense: Classical Variation, Stahlberg Variation

name: Caro-Kann Defense
white: Use e5 for space or develop actively after exchanging. In the Panov, use the isolated pawn for activity.
black: Bring the light-squared bishop outside the pawn chain and challenge White's space with …c5.
mistake: Watch tempi on the developed bishop after h4 or g4.

name: Scandinavian Defense
white: Develop with tempo on the queen and claim central space.
black: After recapturing on d5, retreat the queen safely and build with …c6 and …Bf5 or …Bg4.
mistake: Do not spend repeated moves chasing the queen if it draws your pieces away from useful squares.

name: Pirc Defense
white: Occupy the center, then pick a development plan that can meet a counterattack on e4.
black: Fianchetto, castle, and challenge White's center with …e5 or …c5 at the right moment.
mistake: A broad center can become a target if you push it without piece support.

name: Alekhine Defense
white: Gain space with pawn advances only if you can consolidate and develop.
black: Provoke a large pawn center, then attack its base and retreat the knight to useful squares.
mistake: Counting space as a permanent gain ignores Black's …dxe5 and …c5 breaks.

variations.name: Four Pawns Attack
variations.source: Alekhine Defense: Four Pawns Attack, Tartakower Variation

name: Modern Defense
white: Build a center while keeping the option of Be3, f4, or quieter development.
black: Use the fianchetto to pressure the center, then break with …c5 or …e5.
mistake: Delay central counterplay too long and White can lock in a space advantage.

name: Queen's Gambit Accepted
white: Develop and recover c4 while using the center. Consider e4 if Black allows a broad pawn front.
black: Return the pawn for active development and attack the center with …c5.
mistake: Trying to keep c4 with …b5 can create tactical weaknesses on the queenside.

variations.name: Classical Defense
variations.source: Queen's Gambit Accepted: Classical, Flohr Variation

name: Queen's Gambit Declined
white: Develop pressure on d5 or exchange to reach a Carlsbad structure and plan a minority attack.
black: Develop the kingside, then free the light bishop or time …c5 or …e5.
mistake: Playing only waiting moves can leave the light bishop and queenside cramped.

variations.name: Orthodox Defense
variations.source: Queen's Gambit Declined: Orthodox Defense, Classical Variation

name: Slav Defense
white: Support the center with Nc3 and Nf3. Use a4 when it prevents Black from holding the c4 pawn.
black: Support d5 with …c6, then develop the light bishop before committing …e6 when possible.
mistake: An automatic e3 can lock in White's bishop and give Black time to hold c4.

name: Semi-Slav Defense
white: Choose between a calmer Meran center and sharp variations after Bg5. Calculate tactics on c4.
black: Build the c6–d5–e6 triangle, then free it with …c5 or a queenside expansion.
mistake: The position can open suddenly after …dxc4, so prepare king safety and forcing replies.

variations.name: Meran Variation
variations.source: Semi-Slav Defense: Meran Variation, Sozin Variation

variations.name: Botvinnik Variation
variations.source: Semi-Slav Defense: Botvinnik Variation, Lilienthal Variation

name: London System
white: Develop Bf4 outside the pawn chain, then support d4 with e3 and often c3.
black: Challenge d4 with …c5 or use …Qb6 when the bishop has left b2 unguarded.
mistake: Playing the same setup blindly can lose b2 or miss an early central break.

name: Colle System
white: Develop Bd3 and prepare the e4 break with Nbd2 and c3. The break gives the c1-bishop a role.
black: Challenge d4 with …c5 and compare …b6 with immediate central exchanges.
mistake: Avoid pushing e4 while the center is under-defended.

name: King's Indian Defense
white: Use central space and expand on the queenside if the center locks. Keep watch on your king.
black: Fianchetto, castle, and strike with …e5 or …c5; in a locked center …f5 can create kingside play.
mistake: Thematic pawn storms can fail if the opponent opens a decisive file first.

variations.name: Classical Variation
variations.source: King's Indian Defense: Orthodox Variation, Classical System, Kozul Gambit

variations.name: Fianchetto Variation
variations.source: King's Indian Defense: Fianchetto Variation, Long Variation

name: Queen's Indian Defense
white: Protect e4 and decide whether to meet …Ba6 with b3 or another defense of c4.
black: Use the fianchetto bishop to contest e4. …Ba6 can attack c4 directly.
mistake: Ignoring c4 after …Ba6 can cost a pawn or force awkward defense.

name: Nimzo-Indian Defense
white: Use the bishop pair and center to compensate for structural concessions. Choose how to meet the pin on c3.
black: Pressure e4 and decide if trading on c3 gives Black useful targets.
mistake: Taking on c3 simply because it is available can give White a strong center without a real target.

name: Grünfeld Defense
white: Build the broad pawn center and develop fast enough to keep it.
black: Concede space to attack d4 with the fianchetto bishop and …c5.
mistake: Do not assume that an unchallenged-looking center is safe from …c5 and …Nc6.

variations.name: Exchange Variation
variations.source: Grünfeld Defense: Exchange Variation, Spassky Variation

variations.name: Russian Variation
variations.source: Grünfeld Defense: Russian Variation, Keres Variation

name: Bogo-Indian Defense
white: Meet the bishop check with Bd2 or Nbd2 and build control of e4.
black: Use …Bb4+ to shape White's development and decide whether to trade or defend the bishop.
mistake: Recapturing without considering which piece belongs on d2 can cost tempi.

name: Benoni Defense
white: Use the d5 wedge, e4, and a possible e5 break to exploit central space.
black: Develop Bg7 and seek …b5 or pressure along the e-file. Keep the d6 pawn defended.
mistake: A premature central advance can allow tactics against the uncastled king.

name: Benko Gambit
white: Decide whether to keep the pawn or return it to finish development. Contest the a- and b-files.
black: Trade a pawn for open queenside files, long diagonal pressure, and active rooks.
mistake: A static material count misses the difficulty of defending a2 and b2.

name: English Opening
white: Use c4 to influence d5, then choose a structure based on Black's response.
black: Use …e5 for a reversed Sicilian or …c5 for symmetry. Fight for the center rather than copying indefinitely.
mistake: Ignoring a central break while focusing on flank development can cost space.

name: Réti Opening
white: Use Nf3 and c4 to challenge the center from the flank. Keep flexible transpositions open.
black: Use …d5 and choose whether to advance, defend, or capture on c4 according to development.
mistake: Flank play still depends on central control; do not give it up for a routine fianchetto.

name: Bird's Opening
white: Control e5 with f4 and develop the king's knight. Track the exposed e1–h4 diagonal.
black: Use …d5 for a reversed Dutch structure or challenge with From's Gambit.
mistake: An unprepared kingside pawn push can allow a queen check or an attack on the king.

name: King's Indian Attack
white: Fianchetto, castle, and prepare e4. Choose e5 only when it supports a specific plan.
black: Occupy space and contest e4 or expand on the queenside when White attacks on the king's wing.
mistake: A memorized setup can miss the right moment to contest the center.

name: Budapest Gambit
white: Use development and central control to decide whether the extra pawn is worth holding.
black: Recover e5 with piece activity or force concessions with checks on b4.
mistake: Clinging to e5 while lagging in development can let Black recover the pawn with an attack.

name: Englund Gambit
white: Accept when you can develop with tempo, then calculate …Qb4+ and the pressure on b2.
black: Look for active play after the pawn offer and avoid bringing the queen out without a concrete gain.
mistake: The familiar …Qb4+ trap relies on cooperative replies and is risky against accurate defense.

name: Blackmar-Diemer Gambit
white: Use the half-open f-file and quick development as compensation for the pawn.
black: Develop and secure the king; exchange active pieces if it removes the attack.
mistake: A premature sacrifice on f7 can lose if the rook and queen have no access.

name: Philidor Defense
white: Play d4 to open lines while Black's queenside pieces are undeveloped. If the center opens, look for forcing moves against e8.
black: Support e5 with …d6 and develop your pieces before undertaking a queenside expansion. The Hanham setup reinforces e5 with …Nd7.
mistake: In the Opera Game, …b5 left Black's king in the center and allowed Nxb5 to tear open the position.
